issue.description: Magic numbers in scoring weights (0.4, 0.4, 0.2) and minimum calls threshold (3) reduce readability and configurability
issue.suggestion: Define constants: MIN_CALLS_THRESHOLD = 3, WEIGHT_AVAILABILITY = 0.4, WEIGHT_FIRST_PASS = 0.4, WEIGHT_OVERALL = 0.2

issue.description: Missing docstrings for public functions: gather_events, calculate_metrics, score_and_rank, main lack documentation of params, returns, and side effects
issue.suggestion: Add Google-style or NumPy-style docstrings to all functions

issue.description: Module-level functions (get_latest_tag, iter_commits_since_tag, get_commits_since_tag, parse_changelog_hashes) duplicate GitRepo and ChangelogParser class methods for 'backward compatibility with tests', creating maintenance burden and inconsistency
issue.suggestion: Remove module-level functions; update tests to use class methods directly or patch class methods. If tests require module-level patching, use unittest.mock.patch on class methods

issue.description: main() function is 87 lines with 5 nested functions, violating single responsibility; difficult to test and maintain
issue.suggestion: Extract nested functions to module level or a separate orchestrator class; keep main() as thin entry point

issue.description: collect_commits return type annotation missing type parameter (List instead of List[str])
issue.suggestion: Change to: def collect_commits(latest_tag: str) -> List[str]:

issue.description: get_commits_since_tag loads all commits into memory at once via list(); could OOM on repos with many commits since last tag
issue.suggestion: Use iter_commits_since_tag generator directly in find_missing_entries to stream process; or add --max-commits safety limit

issue.description: print_results returns EXIT_PASS on dry-run even with missing entries; behavior documented but function name suggests it only prints
issue.suggestion: Rename to evaluate_results or split into print_results and determine_exit_code for clarity

issue.description: Two round-trips to database (SELECT then INSERT/UPDATE). Could use single UPSERT statement.
issue.suggestion: Replace with: INSERT INTO ... VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT(fingerprint) DO UPDATE SET last_seen=excluded.last_seen, occurrence_count=occurrence_count+1

issue.description: Three separate queries in get_stats. Could combine into single query with window functions or multiple result sets.
issue.suggestion: Use single query with GROUP BY and window functions, or execute multiple statements in one call

issue.description: Repeated connection boilerplate in is_duplicate, add_or_update, get_stats. Violates DRY, increases bug surface.
issue.suggestion: Create helper function or context manager for database connections, or use a connection pool

issue.description: DB_PATH uses relative path from __file__. Fails if script run from different working directory or if file structure changes.
issue.suggestion: Use absolute path via Path.resolve() or configure via environment variable

issue.description: cleanup_existing_backlog calls init_db() internally, but init_db() also called in main. Redundant and confusing.
issue.suggestion: Remove init_db() from cleanup_existing_backlog; caller should ensure DB initialized

issue.description: ast.walk() visits every node in tree including nested function/class bodies. A NodeVisitor visiting only Import/ImportFrom nodes would be faster.
issue.suggestion: Implement a custom ast.NodeVisitor that only visits Import and ImportFrom nodes, avoiding full tree traversal.

issue.description: Module docstring describes purpose but get_module_name() lacks docstring explaining its cwd assumption and return format.
issue.suggestion: Add docstring to get_module_name: 'Convert filepath to module path relative to project root. Assumes filepath is under Path.cwd(). Returns dotted module path.'

issue.description: Variable `target_base` (filename stem) is used for fuzzy matching but name doesn't convey it's the module basename without extension.
issue.suggestion: Rename to `target_module_basename` or `target_stem` for clarity.

issue.description: Uses os.walk() with string paths while rest of code uses pathlib.Path. Inconsistent path handling.
issue.suggestion: Use Path.rglob('*.py') with filtering, or pathlib.Path.walk() (Python 3.12+). For compatibility: `for filepath in Path('.').rglob('*.py'):` with parent checks.

issue.description: check_assertion prints directly to stdout instead of returning structured results - makes testing and programmatic use difficult
issue.suggestion: Return a dict/dataclass with claim, source, evidence, result and let caller decide output format

issue.description: probe_json_ledger reads entire file into memory with read_text_safe - could be large for jsonl files
issue.suggestion: Process jsonl files line-by-line using open() iterator instead of reading all at once

issue.description: Duplicate status/category counting logic between probe_sqlite_ledger and probe_json_ledger
issue.suggestion: Extract common counting logic into a helper function that accepts an iterable of records

issue.description: inspect_jsonl loads all lines into memory (raw.splitlines()), then all parsed JSON into `parsed` list, then filters to `dict_records` list, then builds key_counts Counter. Three full copies of data in memory for large files.
issue.suggestion: Stream processing: iterate file line by line, parse JSON incrementally, update counters on the fly. Only keep samples (first N records) in memory. Avoid `parsed` and `dict_records` lists entirely.

issue.description: search_source compiles regex pattern on every call (rx = re.compile(pattern)). Called 6 times in main with same patterns. Minor but avoidable recompilation.
issue.suggestion: Pre-compile patterns in SOURCE_GREP_PATTERNS as (compiled_regex, label) tuples, or compile once at module level.

issue.description: schema_of_record truncates dict keys to first 6 sorted keys and list lengths only. For nested structures, this loses significant schema information. The output shows `dict(key1,key2,...)` but not value types.
issue.suggestion: Recursively describe nested schemas with depth limit, or use a library like `jsonschema` inference. At minimum, show value types for dict keys: `dict(key1:str, key2:list[int], ...)`.

issue.description: truncate function uses magic number 100; formatting widths (72, 90, 14, 10, 22, etc.) are hardcoded throughout, making output adjustments difficult
issue.suggestion: Define module-level constants: DEFAULT_TRUNCATE = 100, HEADER_WIDTH = 72, COL_WIDTH = 14, CAT_WIDTH = 22; use consistently

issue.description: Each analysis function (escalation_reasons, tdd_evaluated_outcomes, category_status_matrix, time_series, etc.) iterates over full ledger independently; 6+ full passes over data
issue.suggestion: Compute all aggregates in a single pass: build indices (by_status, by_category, by_file, by_day) once in main(), pass to analysis functions

issue.description: Module-level RuntimeError on import prevents any reuse of helper functions (read_jsonl, parse_ts, truncate) in tests or other tools
issue.suggestion: Move the import guard inside main() or remove it; helper functions are pure and safe to import. If script-only execution is required, guard only the main() call

issue.description: proven_patterns_detail prints all proven records without truncation limit on advisory field in the loop (line 267 uses truncate but line 265 doesn't)
issue.suggestion: Apply truncate consistently: adv = truncate(str(r.get('advisory', '')).strip(), 110) — already done on line 267, but ensure all output fields are bounded

issue.description: main() function is 100 lines with 5 nested functions, mixing argument parsing, validation, collection, parsing, comparison, and reporting; violates single responsibility
issue.suggestion: Extract each nested function to module level with clear signatures; compose in a thin main() orchestrator

issue.description: _size_mb uses path.rglob('*') which recursively traverses all files. On directories with many files (e.g., oracle_queue/pending with thousands of JSON files), this causes significant latency.
issue.suggestion: Cache directory sizes, use os.scandir for non-recursive size, or limit traversal depth. Consider storing size metadata alongside files.

issue.description: Repeated boilerplate for opening/closing SQLite connections in init_db, is_duplicate, add_or_update, and get_stats. Increases maintenance burden and error surface.
issue.suggestion: Create a helper context manager or function (e.g., get_db_connection) that yields a connection and handles commit/rollback/close.

issue.description: Hardcoded directory exclusions (__pycache__, .git, tests) are not configurable. Projects with different structures (e.g., 'test/', 'venv/', '.venv/') will either scan unnecessary dirs or skip needed ones.
issue.suggestion: Define EXCLUDE_DIRS = {'__pycache__', '.git', 'tests', 'test', 'venv', '.venv', 'build', 'dist'} as a module constant and check if any part in Path(root).parts intersects.

issue.description: Functions lack type hints and docstrings. Reduces IDE support and maintainability.
issue.suggestion: Add type hints: `def read_jsonl(p: Path) -> list[dict]:` and docstrings describing parameters, return values, and exceptions.

issue.description: Pattern names defined in ADVISORY_PATTERNS are duplicated in SAFE_CANDIDATES (line 253) and SAFE_ORDER (line 353). Adding/removing patterns requires updating three locations.
issue.suggestion: Define pattern metadata once (e.g., a list of dicts with name, keywords, is_safe, difficulty, order) and derive ADVISORY_PATTERNS, SAFE_CANDIDATES, SAFE_ORDER from it.

issue.description: O(n*m) term matching for each queue item; inefficient for large term lists or queues
issue.suggestion: Precompile a single regex: `pattern = re.compile('|'.join(map(re.escape, _HIGH_RISK_ROUTING_TERMS))); matched = pattern.findall(desc)`

issue.description: read_json reads entire file into memory with `f.read()` before parsing; for large backlog files this can cause MemoryError. json.load(f) streams directly from file handle.
issue.suggestion: Replace lines 44-46 with: `with open(p, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f: return json.load(f), None` (raw not needed; remove raw return or compute separately if required).

issue.description: Nested loop tests every pattern against every line (O(lines * patterns)). With 7 patterns this is manageable, but scales poorly. Each rx.search() call has regex overhead.
issue.suggestion: Combine patterns into a single regex with named capture groups: re.compile('|'.join(f'(?P<{label}>{pat.pattern})' for pat, label in PATTERNS)). Then one search per line with match.lastgroup to identify which pattern matched.

issue.description: Runtime sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT)) modifies global import state. This breaks test isolation, causes flaky imports, and makes the module unimportable without side effects.
issue.suggestion: Restructure to avoid runtime path modification. Either install package in editable mode (pip install -e .) or use relative imports if part of a package.

issue.description: import logging inside conditional branch (line 78) is an anti-pattern. Module-level imports should be at top of file.
issue.suggestion: Move 'import logging' to module imports (line 9). Use logging.getLogger(__name__) at module level.

issue.description: `fake_encode` is defined at module level but only used inside `run_verification`. It references global `calls` and `REQUIRED_DIM`, reducing testability and clarity.
issue.suggestion: Move `fake_encode` inside `run_verification` as a nested function that captures `effective_dim` and a local `calls` list.

issue.description: _load_cases parameter 'test_cases' missing type hint
issue.suggestion: Add type hint: test_cases: list[tuple[str, str, bool]] | None = None

issue.description: validate_config() duplicates Pydantic validation logic - manually checks required keys and types, then load_config() calls Config(**cfg) which re-validates via Pydantic validators
issue.suggestion: Remove validate_config() entirely. Let Pydantic handle all validation by calling Config(**cfg) directly in load_config() and catching ValidationError. Convert ValidationError to RuntimeError.

issue.description: DEFAULT_STRESS_ITERATIONS (10) is hardcoded and not configurable via CLI. Operators cannot adjust iteration count for faster CI runs or more thorough testing without modifying source.
issue.suggestion: Add `--iterations` argument to argparse with default=DEFAULT_STRESS_ITERATIONS, and use `args.iterations` in the loop.

issue.description: verify_chain_memory missing docstring.
issue.suggestion: Add docstring describing parameters, return value, and exceptions.

issue.description: Code contains 'Example IOC detection' comment but is deployed as production logic. Placeholder implementation lacks support for standard IOC types (domains, hashes, URLs, emails, CVEs) required by SOC workflows.
issue.suggestion: Implement a comprehensive IOC extractor using `ioc-finder` library or custom regex registry supporting: IPv4/IPv6, CIDR, domains, FQDNs, URLs, MD5/SHA1/SHA256, email addresses, CVE IDs, registry keys, mutex names, file paths.

issue.description: Duplicate argument definition: '--file' (suppressed) and positional 'input_file' both map to same dest, causing confusion.
issue.suggestion: Remove the suppressed '--file' argument; keep only the positional argument.

issue.description: Multiple imports on single line (ast, json, re, sys) reduces readability and diff clarity
issue.suggestion: Split into separate import lines: import ast; import json; import re; import sys

issue.description: The functions generate_authority_escalation and generate_missing_fields duplicate the base recommendation dictionary logic from generate_valid_baseline, leading to code duplication and maintenance burden.
issue.suggestion: Extract a private helper function `_create_base_recommendation()` that returns a valid base dictionary, and have all generators use it.

issue.description: Duplicate path computation: module-level PROJECT_ROOT/SCHEMA_PATH/LEDGER_PATH and again in _load_config(). Creates drift risk if one is updated and not the other.
issue.suggestion: Remove module-level constants entirely; compute paths only in _load_config() and pass config object to validate_schema/main.

issue.description: verify_payload() performs filesystem I/O directly, making unit testing difficult without temporary files or mocking.
issue.suggestion: Refactor to accept a file-like object or bytes input for the JSON content, separating I/O from validation logic.

issue.description: Hardcoded tool list ["pylint", "bandit"] requires code change to support new tools. Not extensible.
issue.suggestion: Make tool list configurable via environment variable or config file. Iterate over findings_raw.keys() to process all available tools dynamically.

issue.description: LEDGER_PATH hardcoded to ~/Documents/soc-autopilot/overnight/improvement_ledger.jsonl. Not configurable via environment, breaks in containers/different deployments.
issue.suggestion: Read from environment variable (e.g., IMPROVEMENT_LEDGER_PATH) with fallback to current default. Document in deployment docs.

issue.description: Missing type hints, docstrings, and module-level documentation. Function signatures lack return types and parameter types.
issue.suggestion: Add type hints for main() -> None, add docstring explaining purpose, parameters, and side effects. Add inline types for key variables.

issue.description: check_backpressure() lacks detailed docstring documenting parameters, return values, and side effects
issue.suggestion: Add Google-style docstring with Args, Returns, Raises sections

issue.description: check_queue_recovery prints status messages directly, coupling verification logic to console output. This hinders testing, reuse, and structured logging.
issue.suggestion: Return a result object (e.g., tuple of ExitCode and message) and let main() handle printing. Use logging module for structured output.

issue.description: sys.exit(main()) in __main__ block makes the module less testable as a library. While acceptable for a CLI entry point, it prevents importing main() for integration testing without side effects.
issue.suggestion: Keep sys.exit() in __main__ but ensure main() is pure (no side effects beyond I/O) and returns exit code. This is already mostly true; consider documenting that main() is importable for testing.

issue.description: significant code duplication between sanitize_pass() and sanitize_stream(). Both implement nearly identical token processing logic (allowlist check, length guard, entropy calculation, redaction).
issue.suggestion: Extract core token processing logic into a private helper function _process_token(token: str) -> str that returns either the token or REDACTION_TOKEN. Both sanitize_pass and sanitize_stream call this helper.

issue.description: find_forbidden path building logic is fragile and hard to read; uses string concatenation in loop
issue.suggestion: Refactor to use list for path components and join at end: path_parts = []; when descending, append; when found, '.'.join(path_parts) with bracket notation for indices

issue.description: Module-level functions (redact, run_sanitization_check, add_pattern, etc.) duplicate Sanitizer methods, creating maintenance burden and two APIs to keep in sync
issue.suggestion: Deprecate module-level functions in favor of Sanitizer class, or make them thin documented wrappers with clear delegation

issue.description: Spawning separate pytest process for each test file incurs significant overhead; with many auto-generated tests this becomes slow
issue.suggestion: Collect all test files first, then run single pytest --collect-only on all matching files: pytest --collect-only -q tests/test_tdd_auto_*.py, parse output to identify which specific files failed collection

issue.description: Function signature declares `-> bool` but returns `Union[bool, dict]`. Type hint is misleading.
issue.suggestion: Update type hint to `-> Union[bool, dict]` or refactor to return a consistent type.

issue.description: sys.path manipulation makes code fragile to directory structure changes and breaks in packaged deployments
issue.suggestion: Convert to proper package with setup.py/pyproject.toml; use relative imports (from ..alert_pipeline import EnrichedAlert)

issue.description: Multiple imports on one line (os, sys, fcntl, subprocess) violates PEP 8 and makes diff review harder.
issue.suggestion: Split into separate import lines.

issue.description: Building a Counter by loading all lines into memory first is inefficient for large ledgers; streaming line-by-line reduces memory footprint.
issue.suggestion: Iterate over the file object directly: for line in ledger.open(): ...

issue.description: Exit code constants duplicated in main() function (lines 387-390), creating maintenance burden and divergence risk
issue.suggestion: Remove the duplicate constants in main() and use the module-level EXIT_SUCCESS, EXIT_VALIDATION_ERROR, EXIT_CONFIG_ERROR, EXIT_ENV_ERROR

issue.description: Hardcoded source_dirs list requires code change when new source directories are added
issue.suggestion: Discover directories dynamically (e.g., [d.name for d in ROOT.iterdir() if d.is_dir() and not should_skip(d)]) or load from config

issue.description: ALLOWLIST and PATTERNS hardcoded as module constants, preventing runtime configuration without code changes
issue.suggestion: Load patterns and allowlists from config file (JSON/YAML) with fallback to defaults; add --config CLI argument

issue.description: load_api_keys reads and parses .env file on every call with no caching, causing unnecessary I/O
issue.suggestion: Add module-level cache with timestamp; only re-read if file mtime changed or cache expired

issue.description: File is 2518 lines with 50+ functions, multiple global variables, and mixed responsibilities (queue management, fix generation, TDD, forensic analysis, proven/failed memory, scorecard, CLI). Violates single responsibility principle.
issue.suggestion: Split into modules: queue_manager.py, fix_engine.py, tdd_agent.py, forensic_analyzer.py, memory_store.py, scorecard.py, cli.py. Keep self_improver.py as thin orchestrator.

issue.description: _diff_vs_head runs git diff subprocess once per changed file (N+1 calls). For many files this is slow.
issue.suggestion: Batch all paths into a single git diff call: git diff HEAD -- path1 path2 ... for tracked files, and git diff --no-index /dev/null -- path1 path2 ... for untracked.
